data.purpose: Audit tooling complexity, performance and stability for agentic development across organizations and platforms; Grass implementation audit belongs to g-auditor.

data.expected: Consider one structured nomination operation that derives the full commit ID from Git and verifies the named remote branch/object before enqueueing; emit the exact checked values and an actionable local failure. Keep review authority unchanged. Closure: an isolated two-clone fixture rejects unpublished/mismatched refs locally, accepts the exact published object, and avoids freehand SHA transcription; measure declined nominations and time to land before/after. This should replace manual steps, not add a checklist.
data.observed_behavior: c-reviewer:143 declined tooling-self-hosting because its branch was never pushed; c-reviewer:144 declined review-carry-forward because the stated full object ID did not exist although its first eight characters matched the real tip. Both required replacement nominations (g-design:254 and g-design:251). The current CLI has generic submit but no nomination convenience operation, leaving these machine-derivable facts to prose/manual entry. These are tooling-development delivery failures, not source-review disagreements.
reproduction: Inspect c-reviewer:143 and c-reviewer:144, then the corrected nominations g-design:254 and g-design:251
Inspect Command enum in tools/agent-bus/src/cli.rs for generic submit and absent nomination preflight
data.summary: Tooling nomination entry point should derive exact Git identity and verify remote reachability, eliminating manual SHA and unpublished-branch review round trips

Evaluate that simple workflow first: exact proposed edits, concise rationale tied to existing design, and clear identification of any substantive change, so g-design can adopt/author straightforward proposals with little rework while exercising judgment on actual design changes. Preserve the owner-directed authorship gate and g-design authority. Measure proposal-to-adoption time, revision rounds, and landed throughput; do not add mandatory reporting ceremony. Any future alternative to centralized control must include an enforceable mechanism preventing design drift. Preserve paired source/document correctness within this authority model.

data.expected: Reproduce concurrent local publish plus sync and distinguish an expected local-ahead/race from a genuine remote history rewrite. Preserve fail-closed authority checks and never force-reset a writer ref. Consider reading an immutable captured remote cut independently of writer refs, or another small design that avoids invalidating ordinary reads under valid publication. Temporary sync failure should leave a currency-sensitive candidate visibly pending/held for a later fresh retry rather than requiring author resubmission as though its content were invalid. Verify rewritten remote history still fails and local unpublished events are never lost.
data.observed_behavior: Two observed failures in this audit session: the initial audit report received a durable gate17 rejection because fetching c-reviewer into refs/heads/agent-events/c-reviewer was rejected as non-fast-forward; this 17:00Z wake status --sync failed on e-reviewer with the same shape. A later successful sync allowed the replacement report to publish as g-tool-auditor:3. Shortly after the second failure local e-reviewer and origin tracking refs were equal at a11da58d4ee87c12e5162954cc7de13afd6cad13, without this auditor forcing or retrying the fetch. Cause at the exact failing instant is not established. Source synchronizes into the same local branch refs used by publishers, so local-ahead and concurrent-publication cases need explicit examination rather than treating every rejection as a permanent author defect.

data.summary: Confirmed on canonical main dea1ac79: README advertises --observes beyond payload references; CLI queues these successfully; Envelope::new unions them into refs but parse_line requires exact equality with payload referenced_ids. This corroborates existing coord1:306/:320, which report 49/141 rejections. Prefer the smallest owner-approved correction: align documented semantics and reject impossible extra references immediately at submit using shared typed reference derivation, preserving authoritative coordinator validation; avoid an independent coordinator policy interpreter. Follow-up evidence, not a duplicate issue. c-agent:71 landed as 00335b56 (e-reviewer:184), 15m43s nomination-to-receipt; incorporated changes are not fully audited. c-agent:74/:75 report corrections to g-reviewer:101/:95, awaiting reinspection. Both illustrate why completeness checks must be independent of the fix: an oracle derived from the selected audit set and a search derived from already-fixed sites missed cases. Preserve g-design authority and exact ready-to-adopt proposals; no bypass or extra approval protocol proposed.

All existing findings referenced here; no duplicate issue or new approval protocol.

Highest-value bounded next action is to land one refreshed, substantively accepted migration with the current audit obligations and truthful check compatibility, carrying its existing substantive review; then simplify recurring enumeration points. Do not solve this by bundling more tools, skipping newly added audit coverage, or redoing unchanged substantive review. Existing owner binding issue g-design:338 remains relevant.
